title: Global Peace Index 2026 Shows Brazil in 124th Position
seoTitle: Brazil Ranks 124th in Global Peace Index 2026
subtitle: The report reveals the country's position among the 163 evaluated
excerpt: The Global Peace Index 2026, published in June, places Brazil in 124th position among 163 countries, with a score of 2.333.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: O GLOBO, Diário do Centro do Mundo, InfoMoney
contentHtml:
The Global Peace Index 2026, released in June, places Brazil in 124th position among 163 countries and territories, with a score of 2.333. The survey, produced annually by the Institute for Economics and Peace, uses 23 indicators that assess crime, terrorism, violent demonstrations, relations with neighbors, and the political situation.

Why the Topic is Trending Now

The report was published amidst an international scenario of increasing military spending, which reached US$2.9 trillion in 2025, and the highest number of active conflicts since the end of World War II. The global average peace score fell by 0.7% in the last year, marking the 12th consecutive year of deterioration.

Brazil's Position in South America

In the region, Brazil ranks eighth among the 11 countries evaluated. Uruguay leads South America, in 43rd place globally, followed by Chile (52nd) and Paraguay (64th). Argentina appears in 72nd, while Colombia, in 141st, occupies the last South American position.

Comparison with Most and Least Peaceful Countries

Iceland maintains the first position for the 19th consecutive year, with a score of 1.161. New Zealand, Switzerland, Slovenia, and Ireland follow. At the other end, Russia is in the last position, with 3.367 points, followed by Sudan (3.195), Democratic Republic of Congo (3.189), Ukraine (3.184), and Israel (3.124).

Impacts of Global Military Spending

The report highlights that global military spending has increased, reaching US$2.9 trillion in 2025. This rise coincides with an increase in active conflicts, reflecting a trend of deteriorating global peace.

Records of Change Over Time

The survey allows observing how the peace situation has evolved in recent years. Iceland recorded a 2% improvement in its peace level in the last year, while Russia showed a 0.7% improvement, still remaining the least peaceful.

Conclusion on the Current Scenario

The Global Peace Index 2026 offers a clear view of security and stability conditions worldwide. For Brazil, the 124th position places the country in a situation that, although better than the global average, still demands attention to internal issues of crime and political stability.
